# Sources of the Datadog fixtures

Everything under `real/` is copied byte for byte from a public repository. Everything under
`synthetic/` is hand-written by this project and is marked SYNTHETIC in its file name and in a
`_synthetic` key. A test (`tests/test_datadog_fixtures.py`) checks that every file in this tree is
valid JSON and that every `real/` file has a row below with a matching SHA-256, and every
`synthetic/` file is marked.

## Licence

- Repository: https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core, commit `8c5a7ec0d3a0a1d35c694c643cbfa3fd63b94f12` (default branch `master`, fetched 2026-11-11 with `curl` from the codeload tarball; the single file `nginx/assets/monitors/4xx.json` was re-fetched from `raw.githubusercontent.com` at that exact commit and is identical).
- The root `LICENSE` at that commit is the BSD 3-Clause licence ("Copyright (c) 2016, Datadog, Inc.", three conditions: retain notice, reproduce notice in binary form, no endorsement). It contains the "Neither the name of the copyright holder" clause, which is what makes it BSD-3-Clause.
- Every integration's `pyproject.toml` at that commit declares `license = "BSD-3-Clause"` (266 of 269 plain, 3 as `{text = "BSD-3-Clause"}`; none declares another licence). No `LICENSE` file exists inside any integration folder (`nginx/LICENSE` returns 404 at the commit). So the `assets/monitors` and `assets/dashboards` folders carry no separate licence and fall under the root one.
- BSD-3-Clause requires that redistributions of source keep the copyright notice, the list of conditions and the disclaimer. This file and the root licence text satisfy that for the copied JSON; the full licence text is at https://github.com/DataDog/integrations-core/blob/8c5a7ec0d3a0a1d35c694c643cbfa3fd63b94f12/LICENSE. Do not use "Datadog" to endorse a product built from these files.
- Caveat: dashboards and monitors authored by partners may be described in some integrations' `manifest.json` as supported by the partner, not by Datadog. The licence in the repository is still the root one. UNVERIFIED: whether any partner holds additional rights; the repository gives no sign of it.
- These are integration templates (the "monitor template" and "integration dashboard" file shapes), not API exports. A monitor template wraps the API monitor in `{version, created_at, last_updated_at, title, description, tags, definition}`; the API object is under `definition`. A dashboard template is the API dashboard body with `author_name`, `description`, `layout_type`, `template_variables`, `widgets`. The real Datadog API returns more fields (`id`, `creator`, `created`, `modified`, `overall_state`, `matching_downtimes`, ...); the synthetic cases include the API shape.
